overview.description: Gnau, also called Ngau or Ngao, is a Malaysian five-card gambling game using standard French-suited decks and ox-point hand values.

history.origins: Gnau originated in Malaysia and can be played casually or as a gambling game. Each player receives five cards with no discards or redraws, and larger groups can add extra decks.
timeline: Documented card-play form: Gnau is described as a distinct game with its own rules.
history.cultural: Gnau is included because it has a distinct play system rather than being only a title or expansion page.

setup.players: 2 or more players use the table arrangement described for Gnau.
setup.equipment: One or more 52-card French-suited decks, score area, and enough table space for play.
setup.dealing: Deal five cards to every player from one or more standard decks; no redraws or discards are used.

rules.objective: Make a qualifying ox-point hand and compare the resulting value against the dealer or other players.
rules.gameplay: Players inspect five-card hands, identify scoring eligibility, and compare ox-point values under the local payment rules.
keyRules: One or more standard decks may be used.
